data.name: PolicyUsage
data.value:
Usage: localai policy show localai policy set --residency <RequireFullVram|AllowPartialOffload|AllowCpu> localai policy set --idle-model-keep-alive-seconds <non-negative integer> localai policy set --max-embedding-batch <4..256, a power of two> localai policy set --update-check <on|off> localai policy set --update-check-interval-hours <{0}..{1}> localai policy set --language <en|ru|system>
RequireFullVram Models must sit entirely in video memory. Default. AllowPartialOffload Part of a model may spill to system memory. Requires an adapter that holds at least some of it. Slower. AllowCpu Models may run entirely on the CPU. Works without a usable adapter; substantially slower. Idle keep-alive Seconds to keep an idle model loaded. Zero unloads it immediately; 10 by default. Max embedding batch The largest batch a build may grow to on this machine. 256 by default; lower it where the runner drops a request that size, so the build stops re-proving it. Update check Whether this installation may ask GitHub if a newer release exists. Off by default; nothing is ever downloaded or installed without you asking. Language What the CLI and the MCP tools answer in. Follows this computer by default, and falls back to English where there is no translation. Commands and option names are never translated.
data.comment: Usage: and every syntax line are byte-identical in both languages. The description column is 23; a Russian caption longer than 19 characters moves it for all six rows.

data.value: invalid_position: lines and columns are counted from 1; got line {0}, column {1}.
data.comment: Word for word CodeSearchText.PositionNotFromOne, deliberately duplicated: this CLI is what the instruction block offers when that MCP server is unreachable, and the block quotes the sentence as a literal. LocalAi.Cli does not reference CodeSearch.Mcp, so the two cannot share one resource; a test compares them.

data.name: ProfileUnknown
data.value: localai {0} does not know the task profile '{1}'. Supported profiles: {2}
data.comment: Command-agnostic because read-image and translate need the same refusal with a different set, and two parallel keys would drift. No full stop: the line ends in a list somebody copies, the reason HookEventUnknown gives.

data.name: ProgressMinutesLeft
data.value: About {0} min left.
data.comment: Leading space: a clause appended to the line above. Empty on the first unit, where nothing has been measured yet, and never a bare number without about - it is a mean over completed units, and the fallback pass can double it. F1 and invariant, the format IndexBuilder already prints an ETA in. Carried by every counted line - translating a fragment, reading an image - and by ProgressTriageFragment, where the mean is over the log analysed rather than over fragments. In every case the work that follows the last unit, a merge or a retry cascade, is outside the mean: the other reason the sentence says about.

data.name: ProgressPullDownloading
data.value: Downloading {0}: {1} of {2} GB.
data.comment: Two figures and no percent on purpose: the total is summed over the layer digests as they appear, so it can grow, and a percent against a growing denominator moves backwards. Both figures only ever increase. Printed on the silence clock rather than per byte - a byte threshold would encode the connection's speed into the cadence. Three identical lines mean the download has stalled, and that is information.

data.name: ProgressPullPreparing
data.value: Preparing to download {0}: {1} s.
data.comment: The manifest fetch, before any layer size is known. It exists so the run explains why no size is on offer yet.

data.name: ProgressPullStatus
data.value: Ollama reports: {0}. {1} s.
data.comment: Ollama's own status, quoted rather than mapped to one of our phases. Silence here would recreate this defect for every status Ollama adds later. The token is never translated, and it is collapsed to one line and cut to 60 characters before it reaches this sentence.

data.name: ProgressPullStoring
data.value: Adding the model to Ollama: {0} s.
data.comment: After the bytes and the hash: writing the manifest, and removing layers no model needs any more. Minutes on a large model, and silence here reads as a run that finished and then hung.

data.name: ProgressPullVerifying
data.value: Checking what was downloaded: {0} s.
data.comment: Hashing the whole file, after the download line has already reached its own total. Without a line of its own this phase reads as finished-then-hung.

data.name: ProgressQueued
data.value: Waiting in the broker queue: {0} s.
data.comment: Printed only into silence: first at 10 s of a run that has said nothing, then at every 30 s since the last line of any kind. The state is LocalJobState.Queued as the broker client's poll loop reads it, never a guess - a line saying the model is working while the job has not started is the false reassurance this pair exists to refuse.

data.name: ProgressRunning
data.value: The model is working: {0} s.
data.comment: Its pair, for LocalJobState.Running. The number is time in the current state rather than since the command started, so the two lines together read as a timeline. Two variants name the work when the run said what it carries - ProgressRunningImages, ProgressRunningFiles; this is what prints when nothing did.

data.name: ProgressTranslatingFragment
data.value: Translating fragment {0} of {1}.{2}
data.comment: Printed before the call, not after: the total is known before the first one, and it is the fact that decides whether the reader waits. {2} is ProgressMinutesLeft or empty.

data.name: ProgressTranslationRetry
data.value: Translation checks failed ({0}). Retrying with {1}; checkpoint fragments will be reused where available and passing validation.
data.comment: {0} is the validator's detail; {1} is the model tag, which is never translated. Valid checkpoint fragments can be reused during the retry.

data.name: ProgressTriageChoosingModel
data.value: Choosing a model for this log and loading it.
data.comment: Before the capacity probe, which loads a model to find out whether it fits: it unloads others, preflights at a context size and checks residency, stepping down on failure. Minutes of silence otherwise, before anything else about the run can be said.

data.name: ProgressTriageFragment
data.value: Triaging fragment {0}; {1}% of the log analysed.{2}
data.comment: Still no of N: fragments are streamed off the log and that total is not known until it ends. The percent is a denominator that does exist - the position reached in the source against its length - and unlike ProgressPullDownloading's it does not grow, which is why a percent is right here and refused there. It counts what the fragments already analysed covered, so the first line says 0 and no line says 100: the one that says the reading finished is ProgressTriageLogRead. {2} is ProgressMinutesLeft or empty. The seconds since the start are gone from here: the estimate answers what they stood in for, and an index, a percent, an elapsed and an estimate on one line is one figure too many.

data.name: ProgressTriageLogRead
data.value: The whole log is read: {0} fragments.
data.comment: The total, at the first moment it is true. Noun-first in Russian: ResourceManager has no plural support.

data.name: PruneUsage
data.value:
Usage: localai prune [--dry-run]
Applies the retention bounds in one pass: superseded index generations and the overlay sets under them, overlays for commits and worktrees nothing is on any more, the whole record of a repository whose checkout is gone or whose first indexing never finished, finished broker jobs and the answers stored with them, quarantined entries, telemetry past its retention, installed versions beyond the {0} kept, and installer backups.
Kept whatever the bounds say: the generation each repository is answered from now, the overlay every existing worktree is on now, the running version, and any job a client may still be collecting. This installation keeps at least {1} generation(s) per repository.
--dry-run Report what would go, and remove nothing.
Everything named above is under {2}.
data.comment: Usage: and the option name are byte-identical in both languages. Both counts are holes fed from the retention policy this installation reads, so the block cannot name a bound the code does not apply. The list is deliberately complete: shortening it would understate what a run removes.

data.value: The model is working on {0} image(s): {1} s.

One call carries every image, so there is nothing inside it to count: what is missing is not a position but the size of what was sent, which is the fact that says whether forty seconds is ordinary. A per-image counter was the alternative and it lies - the images are encoded in about a second and the model then works for minutes, so the counter stops at the last one and reads as a hang there. data.comment: Compared by branch name rather than by path: the command may be run from a worktree, and the branch checked out there is the one it must not delete.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptNoCommits

data.comment: A branch created a moment ago sits exactly on the mainline, so the containment check says "merging it would change nothing" about it too. Without this it would be the first thing the command deleted.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptUnmerged
data.value: Branch {0} was kept: {1} commit(s) of its own are not in {2}.
data.comment: The ordinary case, and the count is what makes it checkable by hand. Reached when merging the branch would change the mainline's tree.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptDirty
data.value: Branch {0} was kept: its worktree {1} still holds changes that are not committed.
data.comment: The tail is AgentWorktreeHoldsWork's, word for word, so one machine cannot describe the same worktree two ways. Names no flag, because there is none.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptLocked
data.value: Branch {0} was kept: its worktree {1} is locked.
data.comment: git worktree lock is how a person says "leave this one alone", and this command is one of the things they were saying it to.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptWorktreeUnreadable
data.value: Branch {0} was kept: the state of its worktree {1} could not be read ({2}).
data.comment: Covers the case PruneCommand.IsGone exists for: a worktree on an unmounted volume or a disconnected share reads exactly like one deleted by hand, and taking that as deleted would drop a branch whose work nobody looked at.

data.name: RepoPruneKeptUnanswerable
data.value: Branch {0} was kept: whether {1} already has it could not be established ({2}).
data.comment: Reached when git merge-tree exits non-zero — a conflict, a ref it will not merge, or a git too old for --write-tree, whose message ({2}) says which. Says it could not be established rather than that the branch is unmerged: this command must not report a comparison it did not make.

data.name: RepoPruneWorktreeRefused
data.value: Worktree {1} of branch {0} could not be removed ({2}), so the branch was kept.
data.comment: git refuses to delete a branch held by a worktree, so the order is forced: the worktree first. A branch kept because its worktree survived is the honest outcome, not a failure to report separately.

data.name: RepoPruneBranchRefused
data.value: Worktree of branch {0} was removed, but the branch itself was not ({1}).
data.comment: The half-done state, and the only line that reports it. Printed on the hook face too: a tree left half-cleaned must be visible on the pull that did it.

data.name: RepoPruneSummary
data.value: Removed {0} branch(es) and {1} worktree(s).
data.comment: Counts rather than a list: the lines above already named each one.

data.name: RepoPruneWouldSummary
data.value: Nothing was removed. A run without --dry-run would remove {0} branch(es) and {1} worktree(s).
data.comment: Opens by saying nothing happened, because a summary of deletions is the line most likely to be read on its own.

data.name: RepoPruneNothing
data.value: Nothing was removed: no branch here is fully in {0}.
data.comment: True when no branch qualified and true when the mainline is the only branch there is, so one key covers both. A count of branches examined would read as "of the 0 branch(es)" on the common case.

data.name: RepoPruneMainlineMissing
data.value: Nothing was removed: this repository has no local mainline branch to compare against. None of these exists here: {0}
data.comment: Not MainlineMissing, whose sentence ends "before indexing" — the wrong reason on this command. {0} is the refs actually tried, starting with the manifest's own DevRef.

data.name: RepoPruneUnknownArgument
data.value: localai repo prune does not understand '{0}'. Nothing was removed. Usage: {1}
data.comment: Shaped after PruneUnknownArgument: like localai prune, an argument this command silently ignored would delete, so the refusal says what did not happen as well as what was not understood.

data.name: RepoPruneDryRun
data.value: --dry-run: nothing was removed; the branches and worktrees below are what a run without it would remove.
data.comment: First line, not last, for the reason PruneDryRun is: a notice at the end of a report of deletions is read after them.

data.name: RepoPruneAutomationOffer
data.value: To do this after every pull that brings work into the mainline: git config localai.pruneMerged true
data.comment: Printed only after a hand run that removed something and only while localai.pruneMerged is unset — the moment the reader has just seen what the setting would do. The setting is off until a repository asks for it: an installed hook was invited to keep an index in sync, not to delete branches. No trailing full stop: the line ends in a command somebody copies.

data.name: RepoPruneRootWithoutDirectory
data.value: localai repo prune --root requires a directory.
data.comment: Shaped after the same refusal on repo status.

data.name: RepoPruneUsage
data.value:
Usage: localai repo prune [--root dir] [--dry-run]
Removes what a merged pull request leaves behind in this repository: a local branch whose every commit is already in the mainline branch, and the worktree that branch was checked out in. A run that removed something then applies this repository's index retention, exactly as localai sync does at the end of every synchronisation.
A branch goes only when all of these hold: it is not the mainline branch and not the branch this command is running on; it carries at least one commit of its own; merging it into the mainline would change nothing; and its worktree, if it has one, is not locked and holds no change and no untracked file. Every other branch is listed with the reason it was kept.
Nothing here reaches the network, and no branch is deleted on any remote.
--root dir The repository to work on. The current directory by default. --dry-run List what would go, and remove nothing.
To keep a worktree whatever its branch: git worktree lock <path>
data.comment: Printed on --help and nowhere else. Multi-line on purpose: the conditions under which a branch is deleted are what a person needs before they run this once, and a one-line usage cannot carry them.
